clue.text: 'Recover' financially

parts.note: read the quoted word as re-cover, to cover again, and the money sense is taking out a second insurance policy on a risk

explanation.surface: Someone getting their finances back on track.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks invite you to split the word: re-cover means cover again, which in finance is what an insurer does when it passes on part of a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer that offloads part of its risk to another company buys cover again, which is literally covering anew in a financial sense.

clue.text: Strong vehicle ploughing into rubbish

indicators.note: ploughing into says the vehicle is driven inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sturdy truck crashes into a heap of garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means sturdy, tough and hardy.

clue.text: Again comedian collects money for work

indicators.note: collects says the phrase gathers the letters within it

explanation.surface: A comedian is paid for a gig yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is earnings, the pay one receives for one's labour.

clue.text: Team's method for providing incidental entertainment

parts.note: a side is a team, so the team's is the side's
how is the method or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A team's way of putting on some extra fun at the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a minor attraction at a fair or circus, a diversion from the main event.

clue.text: Queues increased, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: rose means went up, increased

explanation.surface: People hear that the lines are getting longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows are lines of people or things, so lines waiting their turn.

clue.text: Soldier caught in passage runs

indicators.note: in puts the caught abbreviation inside the word for a passage

parts.note: a lane is a narrow passage or way
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A soldier trapped in a corridor makes a run for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer is a cavalryman armed with a lance, a kind of soldier.

clue.text: An American gangster ensnaring one maiden, the beast!

indicators.note: ensnaring says the letters for one and maiden are caught inside the other words

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal American gangster
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A mobster traps a young girl, the brute!
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a creature or brute; the exclamation also calls someone brutish.

clue.text: Bellowed a formula for making cider

parts.note: read as wordplay, the letters of cried with out as an anagram signal would give the drink cider

explanation.surface: Someone shouted a recipe for brewing cider.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay. Take CRIED and treat OUT as the anagram signal, and you get CIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout loudly, to roar or yell, is to cry out.

clue.text: Ferocious creature turning up to gather soldiers in military unit

indicators.note: to gather says the reversed creature wraps around the soldiers
turning up in a down clue means the big cat's letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tiger is a fierce animal
men means soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A wild beast shows up and herds the troops of an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' fits a down clue, where the creature reads upwards as REGIT; the soldiers sit inside that. 'Ferocious creature' tempts toward lion, but only the striped cat fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent unit of an army, typically commanded by a colonel.

clue.text: Concede defeat with player injured?

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
down means hurt and lying on the ground, out of action

explanation.surface: A team gives up the match after one of its players gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby a back is a defender; 'down' as in a player who is down and needs treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is an idiom for retreating from a position or giving in.

clue.text: Trying to be excellent party leader once

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
Ming is Sir Menzies Campbell, formerly leader of the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A politician once strove to lead the party brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, with the digit read as the letter I. Menzies 'Ming' Campbell led Britain's Liberal Democrats in 2006-07.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiming at something means attempting or striving to achieve it.

clue.text: Second fiddle with very difficult task

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle about with something

explanation.surface: A second violinist is given a hard job.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is informal for something awkward or nasty, such as a hard exam.

clue.text: Urgent appeal going round in the morning to get a bit of food

indicators.note: going round says the distress call is wrapped around the abbreviation for the morning

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, an urgent call for help
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: An early-morning plea for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a small fried pastry with a spiced filling, an Indian snack.

clue.text: A confused don enters a vehicle arbitrarily

indicators.note: enters says the jumbled letters go inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails in the street

indicators.note: confused means the letters of don are muddled

explanation.surface: A bewildered university lecturer boards a tram without any plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes NDO from the university fellow, and 'enters' lodges it in the vehicle; 'a' before 'vehicle' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no plan or pattern is acting haphazardly, without choice or reason.

clue.text: When going round south Africa meadow, see shrubs

indicators.note: going round says the word for when encloses the other letters

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
ZA is the international code for South Africa
a lea is a meadow, poetically

explanation.surface: Travelling around a South African meadow, take a look at the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Azaleas are flowering bushes of the rhododendron family.

clue.text: Show disapproval of flavour, drinking

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
zing is a lively, zesty taste

explanation.surface: Jeering at the taste while having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozing is informal for drinking alcohol heavily.

clue.text: Spoil game at home

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Bad weather spoils a home fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck or destroy it.

clue.text: Put out a list — ABC of rock

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone publishes a list, the basics of geology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' rearranges A LIST and ABC.
explanation.definitionFit: Basaltic describes something made of basalt, a dark volcanic stone.

clue.text: Lambasting for what sounds like a second-class grade

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a B rating is a second-class grade, one below A

explanation.surface: Someone is given a dressing-down for getting only a B.
explanation.definitionFit: Berating is scolding angrily, giving someone a telling-off.

clue.text: Get rid of plane? It's flying on

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: flying means the letters of it's are tossed into a new order before on is added

explanation.surface: A pilot ditches the aircraft as it carries on in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges IT'S into TIS; the apostrophe is ignored, and 'Get rid of plane?' reads as ditching an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw cargo overboard, to discard.

clue.text: Middle east location : a place for thieves?

parts.note: a den of thieves is the stock phrase for a robbers' hideout

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern city is labelled a hideout for robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Done with a warm garment on

explanation.surface: A person finishes wrapping up in warm clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being done means cheated out of money; wearing a fleece jacket means being clad in a fleece.

clue.text: Packet of great weight at back of vehicle

indicators.note: at back of says the heavy weight comes after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A heavy load stowed at the rear of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a light box or container, such as one holding milk or eggs.

clue.text: Male in work? Not an important one

indicators.note: work, as a verb, means the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A man at his job is told he is a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male in work' looks like a man employed; 'work' is the signal to rearrange MALE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a lowly servant, someone doing humble chores.

clue.text: Skirt gets drink stain at the top

indicators.note: at the top in a down clue puts the stain above the drink

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blemish
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A skirt gets a gin stain on the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' is not clothing: as a noun it means an edge or border.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt can mean the outer edge or border of something, like the edge of a page.

clue.text: A loony woman beginning to tickle a bird

parts.note: loony means crazy, mad
Ava is a woman's name

indicators.note: beginning to says only the first letter of tickle is used

explanation.surface: A crazy woman starts tickling a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The amadavat is a small red waxbill finch from South Asia, often kept as a cage bird.

clue.text: Goddess making appearance in America, then Asia

indicators.note: making appearance in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deity turns up first in the Americas and then in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek deity of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: In favour of keeping university square

indicators.note: keeping says the word for in favour of holds the university letter

parts.note: for means in favour of

explanation.surface: Supporting a university quad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is a number here: two times two.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is a perfect square number, being two multiplied by itself.

clue.text: The dirty newspaper boss got rid of a number

indicators.note: got rid of says the editor's letters are taken out of the words before

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor sacks a number of grubby reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty is the cardinal figure three times ten.

clue.text: Enclosure around kiln that's very hot

indicators.note: around says the word for an enclosure goes round the kiln

parts.note: a ring is a circular enclosure, as in a boxing or circus ring
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A fenced area around a hop kiln that gives off great heat.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST (oast house) is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting is informal for sweltering, uncomfortably warm.

clue.text: Powerful chap taken on by firm

indicators.note: taken on by says the chap comes after the firm, as if hired by it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a gent is a man, a chap

explanation.surface: A strong man is hired by a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and convincing.

clue.text: American presenting forthright policy with no place for English

parts.note: frank means outspoken, forthright

indicators.note: with no place for says the English abbreviation is dropped from the word for policy

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A plain-speaking US politician whose policy leaves no room for the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was a founding father of the United States.
